Homemade toaster pastries

When I was small, I thought breakfast pastries came from a magical factory. This is a long, chatty introduction about childhood, about the oven, about trying 3 times before getting it right.

Below you will find a pastry and two filling options; pick one.

Homemade toaster pastries

Pastry
2 cups (250 grams) all-purpose flour
1 tablespoon sugar
1 teaspoon salt
1 cup (225 grams) cold unsalted butter
1 large egg
2 tablespoons milk

Cinnamon filling
½ cup (100 grams) brown sugar
1 ½ teaspoons ground cinnamon
1 tablespoon flour

Or, jam filling (alternative)
¾ cup jam
1 tablespoon cornstarch mixed with 1 tablespoon cold water

To finish
1 large egg, beaten, to brush on pastry

Make the pastry: Whisk the flour, sugar and salt. Work in the butter until it looks like coarse crumbs, then stir in the egg and milk until the dough comes together.

Roll and cut: Divide the dough in half, roll each into a 9 by 12 inch rectangle and cut each into nine rectangles.

Fill: Brush half the rectangles with egg, spoon a heaping tablespoon of the filling you chose into the centre, top with the remaining rectangles and seal the edges with a fork.

Bake: Bake at 350°F for 20 to 25 minutes, until golden.

Do ahead: Unbaked pastries keep, frozen, for up to a month.
